title: session-router: compact session facade, credential warmup & unified backoff across Py/TS/Go
author: Maya Hernandez
description:
Context & motivation: We have a recurring class of issues where long-lived streaming clients suffer higher tail-latency or transient 401/403 churn during cold-starts and credential rotations. In addition, SDK ergonomics around stream consumers and typed iterables have divergent shapes across Python/TS/Go, causing integration friction for cross-platform teams. This PR introduces a compact, language-agnostic 'session-router' facade idea implemented as adapters in each SDK: it centralizes warmup (proactive credential handshakes), a small router for session affinity (prefer warmed sessions), and a unified backoff matrix so SDKs share retry semantics across reconnects and reauth flows.

What this PR does: - Adds session-router adapter implementations in python/ts/go SDK packages (lightweight, opt-in). - Implements credential warmup: a non-blocking prefetch+handshake that reduces first-request auth churn. - Introduces a unified backoff profile matrix (fast/medium/steady) used by streaming reconnect + token refresh flows; profiles are bridged to native timers/loop constructs per SDK. - Polishes streaming iterable ergonomics: typed cursors in TS, async context manager for Python streams, and a Pause/Resume handle for Go. - Bumps SDK package versions: python->0.9.1, typescript->1.6.0, go->1.5.3 and updates cross-sdk interop tests. - Adds migration notes and a small sample that demonstrates graceful session handoff when rotating credentials.

Checklist: - [x] Session-router spec and simple diagram added to docs - [x] Adapter implementations in python/ts/go - [x] Unit + integration tests for warmup and backoff transitions - [x] Version bumps and release notes - [x] E2E smoke tests against canary runtime

Commits (summary): - 9f2b1d0: spec(session-router): initial design doc + diagrams - c3ab4e7: feat(py): session-router adapter + async stream context manager - d7f4a33: feat(ts): stream facade + typed cursor / backoff wiring - b1a2c8f: feat(go): session adapter + pause/resume handle - 5e8c0e4: test: add interop e2e matrix and warmup assertions - 7aa4ff1: ci: fix gofmt and lint failures reported in first CI run - 2d3b9a5: docs: migration notes and examples - 4f6b22c: chore(release): bump versions 

High-level files changed (representative): - sdk/python/redwood/session_router.py (new) - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/context.py (changed) - sdk/python/setup.cfg / pyproject.toml (version bump) - sdk/typescript/src/session/router.ts (new) - sdk/typescript/src/stream/typed_cursor.ts (changed) - sdk/typescript/package.json (version bump) - sdk/go/session/router.go (new) - sdk/go/stream/handle.go (changed) - sdk/common/backoff/profiles.go|ts|py (new cross-sdk profiles) - tests/e2e/session_warmup_matrix.test (new) - docs/sdk/session-router.md (new) - scripts/verify-version-sync.sh (changed)

Testing & CI: - Initial CI run failed on gofmt and a flaky TS linter rule (max-line-length in generated docs). Fixes were pushed in commit 7aa4ff1. - Full CI (unit + integration + e2e matrix) passed on the final push: all checks green. - Added a short-lived job to run the canary runtime against this branch for 12 hours; smoke metrics showed ~34% reduction in first-minute reauth errors for workloads with short-lived credentials.

Review thread (high level): - Ethan Cole (review): asked for clearer failure modes if warmup fails (auth server 5xx). Response: fallback behavior added: warmup is best-effort; on failure clients fall back to normal on-demand auth with exponential backoff and a per-session failure counter surfaced via telemetry. - Priya Nambiar (security): requested KMS/HSM flow be validated for Private deployments. Response: added unit test for KMS-backed token provider and documented HSM caveats in migration notes. - Luca Romano (perf): asked for measurements and added a request to gate warmup default to opt-in. Response: warmup default set to opt-out in this PR; runtime teams will enable warmup on canaries before flipping default.

Migration notes & developer impact: - For most users this is opt-in: set session_router.enabled = true in SDK config to activate warmup and session affinity. - If you rely on exact retry timing, confirm behavior against the new backoff profiles (fast/medium/steady) and override with explicit config if needed. - Breaking changes: none expected; streaming iterables have additive ergonomic helpers only.

Release notes (short): Introduce session-router adapter with credential warmup, unified backoff matrix, better streaming consumer ergonomics and cross-sdk version bumps (py 0.9.1, ts 1.6.0, go 1.5.3). Opt-in feature; reduces first-minute auth churn for short-lived creds.

Merge: squash-and-merge by Priya Nambiar after final sign-off.

release_notes: Introduce session-router adapter (opt-in) providing credential warmup, session affinity, and a unified backoff profile across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Version bumps: py 0.9.1, ts 1.6.0, go 1.5.3. Reduces transient first-minute auth failures for short-lived credentials.
